newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks climb to record heights at open.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks climb to record heights at open.

* Toronto stocks climbed further into uncharted territory at the open on Thursday as transportation and conglomerate stocks soared.
* 6.1 million shares traded worth C$111.5 million.
Toronto stocks climbed further into uncharted territory at the open on Thursday in quiet trade as transportation and conglomerate stocks soared.

The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index rose 15.12 points to 6780.28 in turnover of 6.1 million shares worth C$111.5 million. Advancing stocks outnumered decliners 220 to 170, while 223 issues traded unchanged.
Traders said a few strong issues were holding the market in positive territory as the heavily weighted gold and banking sectors fell.

The transport group was up 3.11 percent as Canadian National Railway Co jumped 6 in early trading before settling down to trade 4.40 higher at 71.50. CNR said late Wednesday it expected to meet its key 1997 operating ratio target of 83 percent.
Conglomerates gained 152 points or 1.65 percent on the strength of Canadian Pacific Ltd, up 0.75 at 42.85.

CP on Wednesday reported second quarter earnings of C$0.70 per share, compared to US$0.53 per share in the same period last year. Golds led the weak side, shedding 99.5 points or 1.23 percent, while banks fell 48.1 points or 0.65 percent.
--- HOT STOCKS ---
* Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce fell 0.70 to 39 in healthy trade after rising earlier this week on news that the bank agreed to buy U.S. brokerage Oppenheimer & Co for US$525 million.
"I think that (CIBC) kind of got ahead of itself with all the stuff about Oppenheimer," one trader said.
